sections.title: About ADAA
sections.text: The Anxiety and Depression Association of America (ADAA) is an international nonprofit organization dedicated to the prevention, treatment, and cure of anxiety, depression, OCD, PTSD, and related disorders. Founded in 1979, ADAA works to improve the lives of millions of people affected by these conditions through education, research funding, and support for mental health professionals and the public.

sections.title: Educational Resources
sections.text: ADAA provides extensive free educational resources including articles, webinars, podcasts, and videos about anxiety disorders, depression, and related conditions. Topics cover symptoms, treatment options, self-help strategies, and the latest research findings. Resources are written and reviewed by mental health professionals and help people understand their conditions and make informed treatment decisions.

sections.title: Find a Therapist Directory
sections.text: ADAA maintains a searchable directory of licensed mental health professionals who specialize in treating anxiety disorders and depression. You can search by location, specialty, and treatment approach including cognitive-behavioral therapy (CBT), exposure therapy, and medication management. All listed providers have expertise in evidence-based treatments for anxiety and mood disorders.

sections.title: Online Peer Support Community
sections.text: ADAA offers a moderated online peer support community where people with anxiety and depression can connect, share experiences, and support each other. The community provides a safe space to discuss challenges, celebrate progress, and feel less alone. Members can participate in discussion forums, read personal stories, and access peer-driven resources.

sections.title: For Mental Health Professionals
sections.text: ADAA supports mental health professionals through continuing education opportunities, research grants, and an annual conference that brings together leading researchers and clinicians. The organization publishes the peer-reviewed journal Depression and Anxiety and provides resources to help clinicians deliver evidence-based treatment for anxiety and mood disorders.
